To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Basilea rabbits produce antibodies with λ chains; (2) these chains are structurally heterogeneous, as shown by the presence of two different N-terminal amino acid sequences, one of which is similar to k chains; (3) the repertoire of Vλ chain genes is large, similar to that of k genes; (4) the response to pneumococcal polysaccharide antigens is of high magnitude and polyclonal, and (5) the response is independent
Basilea rabbits produce antibodies with λ chains that are structurally heterogeneous, and that the repertoire of Vλ chain genes appears to be large and comparable to that of Vκ chains.
the immune response of Basilea rabbits (lacking k light chains) is similar to that of standard rabbits (producing k light chains) with respect to the magnitude and heterogeneity of the response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the immune response in the rabbit.
the molecular basis of immunologic diversity.
the study of the structure of the antibody response in rabbits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Basilea variant rabbit is not a good model for the mouse λ system, but that it is rather similar in its L chain structure and repertoire to standard rabbits.
in Basileas the V λ repertoire is large and of a size comparable to that of V k.

in Basileas, as in standard rabbits, the L chain repertoire is large and the L chain response is highly polyclonal, thus supporting the concept of the existence in both species of a large number of L chain genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the existence of several V λ genes in Basilea and that they can be expressed in the same animal in the same antibody response.
the repertoire of the λ chain in rabbits is as large as that of the κ chain and that the λ chain genes are expressed in the rabbit as well as in the mouse.
Basilea rabbits are an excellent model to study the immune response in the absence of a specific L chain subgroup.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel mechanism of action of the anti-inflammatory drug, celecoxib, that may be responsible for its anti-cancer effects in patients.
